name: FL-19
label: Likely R

key_factors: District leans Republican by 14 points, and the open seat does not change that
Schwartzel holds a roughly 35-to-1 fundraising edge over Arias
Prediction markets price a Republican win at about 94%
No public general-election polling, keeping uncertainty elevated
model.rationale: The seat's strong Republican lean, Schwartzel's dominant fundraising, and market pricing near 94% for the GOP all point the same direction; with no public polling, uncertainty stays wide, but the evidence leaves Arias only a narrow path.
model.watch: Heavy Democratic outside spending, a scandal involving Schwartzel, or a surprise poll showing a single-digit race would justify moving this toward tossup territory.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Byron Donalds (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Byron Donalds is leaving the seat to run for governor, producing an open contest in a southwest Florida district that leans Republican by about fourteen points. Jim Schwartzel enters the general election as the clear favorite, having raised more than two million dollars to Democrat Victor Arias's roughly fifty-eight thousand. Prediction markets give Schwartzel about a ninety-four percent chance of winning, and no expert ratings cover the race.

The open seat removes any incumbency cushion, but the district's fundamental lean dominates. No public general-election polls are available, which keeps uncertainty wider than in well-polled contests, and Arias has little money to alter the dynamic. Unless outside groups invest heavily on the Democratic side or an unexpected development hits Schwartzel, the seat is expected to remain in Republican hands.
